text:
The City Council convened to address Item 9, a recommendation from City Manager Thomas Modica to amend his employment agreement. The amendment permits Modica to voluntarily participate in the citywide work furlough program under the same terms and conditions as other city employees. Modica explained that this measure ensures shared sacrifice across the entire city staff during a difficult financial period. He clarified that he would remain available for emergencies and matters that cannot be reasonably delayed.

Council members expressed strong support for the proposal. Councilmember Austin thanked Modica for stepping up and emphasized the importance of shared sacrifice, noting a desire for the council to participate in similar measures. Councilmember Richardson and other members echoed this sentiment, praising the City Manager for uniting with city employees. The Mayor reiterated the body’s interest in ensuring all organizational members, including elected officials, undergo equivalent furlough cuts.

Modica informed the council that a separate item regarding the participation of elected officials in the furlough program is currently under final research due to charter complexities. He stated that this item would be presented for consideration on September 8. Following the discussion, the council conducted a roll call vote, and the motion to amend the agreement carried.

The meeting then transitioned to general public comment on non-agenda items. A speaker began addressing topics related to systemic racism, equity, and violence prevention, but technical difficulties prevented the council from hearing the full statement. The clerk and staff attempted to resolve the audio issues, but the speaker was unable to continue effectively. Consequently, the council decided to proceed with the remaining agenda items, specifically Item 6, a communication from Councilmembers Pearce, Zendejas, Price, and Richardson recommending the receipt and filing of a presentation from the Clean Power Alliance on Community Choice Aggregation. The council planned to return to the general public comment session once the technical issues were resolved.
